questions.question: A generative model is trained on samples from an unknown distribution. What should it learn to do?
options: Assign each training sample to a fixed class
Recover the exact source label for every sample
Compress every sample without learning a sampler
Produce new samples resembling the training distribution
questions.explanation: A generative model learns a sampler whose new outputs resemble draws from the unknown data distribution. Assigning fixed labels classifies existing examples, but does not provide a process for producing new samples.

questions.question: What can an explicit-density model do that an implicit GAN-style sampler cannot?
options: Map noise into a realistic output
Evaluate how likely a particular point is
Generate a sample in one forward pass
Condition a sample on a class label
questions.explanation: An explicit-density model exposes a tractable value such as log p(x), allowing a query about a point’s likelihood. An implicit GAN-style generator can sample, but has no density evaluation to return.

questions.question: Which family optimizes a lower bound on log p(x) rather than an exact likelihood?
options: Autoregressive models with exact factorization
Normalizing flows using invertible transforms
GANs using an implicit discriminator
VAEs using an ELBO objective
questions.explanation: VAEs optimize an ELBO, a lower bound on log p(x), rather than an exact likelihood. Autoregressive factorization and invertible normalizing flows are the lesson’s tractable explicit-density families.

questions.question: What happens before a token-based autoregressive model generates high-dimensional data?
options: A discriminator assigns every pixel a realness score
A score model predicts a continuous density gradient
A tokenizer compresses it into discrete codes
A flow maps each sample to a Gaussian exactly
questions.explanation: Token-based autoregressive generation first compresses high-dimensional data into a shorter sequence of discrete codes, then models that sequence. A score model predicts a continuous log-density gradient rather than discrete tokens.

questions.question: A service needs exact log-likelihood values for density estimation and does not need samples. Which family does the lesson recommend?
options: StyleGAN with a fixed-domain generator
GANs with a fast implicit sampler
Diffusion with iterative denoising
Normalizing flows with tractable likelihood
questions.explanation: For density estimation without sampling, the use table recommends normalizing flows because their invertible transformations provide exact log p(x). A GAN’s fast implicit sampler cannot answer the likelihood query.

questions.question: A narrow face-generation product values a single fast forward pass. Which model family fits the lesson’s inference comparison?
options: A flow model with an autoregressive decoder
A GAN with one generator forward pass
A diffusion model with many denoising steps
A VAE with repeated latent refinement
questions.explanation: A GAN generates by one forward pass through its generator, which suits a narrow face domain needing low latency. Diffusion instead runs an iterative denoising schedule, adding repeated inference steps.
